title: SDK-based MCP server (mcp_server.py) is non-functional dead code
evidence: brazilian_soccer_mcp/mcp_server.py:11 `import mcp.server.stdio` raises ImportError: cannot import name 'TypeAdapter' from 'pydantic' (pydantic v1 in-env, mcp needs v2); line 589 `default_server = BrazilianSoccerMCPServer()` at import time; 19 `@self.server.call_tool()` decorators (lines 53-324) all register the SDK's single global call_tool handler so only the last survives; `list_tools` appears 0 times so get_tools() (line 342) is never wired to a list_tools handler; .coverage shows mcp_server.py line_bits=0 (0% coverage, never imported by tests).
suggestion: Pin pydantic>=2, register one @server.list_tools() returning get_tools() and one @server.call_tool() that dispatches by name, and add an import/smoke test. R1 is still satisfied by server.py, but this module ships broken.

title: Two parallel server implementations (server.py + mcp_server.py)
evidence: brazilian_soccer_mcp/server.py:19 BrazilianSoccerMCP (string-method dispatcher over the 19 query handlers, tested by TestServerAPI) and brazilian_soccer_mcp/mcp_server.py:25 BrazilianSoccerMCPServer (MCP SDK variant) duplicate the same 19 tool bodies; only server.py is exercised.
suggestion: Collapse to one server: keep the SDK transport as the entrypoint delegating to the shared query engines, or delete the unused/broken variant.

title: Coverage 0.68 dragged down by uncovered 593-line mcp_server.py
evidence: scores.json test_coverage=0.68 while defect_rate=1.0 (all 41 tests pass, 0 skips); mcp_server.py (593 lines, ~22% of package) has 0% coverage per .coverage line_bits.
suggestion: Either test or remove mcp_server.py; the functional code (server.py + engines) is otherwise well covered.
